observations: Three photos show a foldable smartphone in an open box, flanked by two boxes with Google branding and a 'G' logo.
The phone has a large, unfolded screen with a visible interface (photo 2), and a rear camera module with two large lenses and a smaller sensor (photos 0 and 1).
The phone's back is light blue or grey with a 'G' logo (photos 0 and 1).
The boxes are white with a 'G' logo and an outline of a phone with a dual-camera setup (photos 0 and 1).
The background wall has large black letters spelling 'GENUINE DEVICES PLUG' (all photos).
A white charging cable is visible in front of the phone (photos 0 and 2).
Photo 2 shows the phone's screen on, displaying a home screen with widgets and apps, suggesting it is powered on and functional.
No model name or number is visible on the phone or boxes in any photo.

claims.claim: Premium uk used Google pixel 10 pro fold 256gb physical + eSIM
claims.evidence: No such model as 'Pixel 10 Pro Fold' exists. Google has not released a 'Pixel 10' series. The phone shown resembles the Pixel Fold, but no model name is visible. The claim is factually incorrect.

risks.risk: The phone may be a counterfeit or a different model misrepresented as a 'Pixel 10 Pro Fold'.
risks.proof: A clear shot of the phone's settings menu showing the model name, or a close-up of the box with the model printed on it.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic foldable smartphone, not as a premium Pixel model.

risks.risk: The phone may have screen damage, hinge issues, or software problems not visible in the photos.
risks.proof: A video showing the phone folding and unfolding smoothly, and a full screen test with no dead pixels or creases.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially defective or with hidden damage.

risks.risk: The phone may not be unlocked or may have carrier restrictions, despite claiming 'physical + eSIM'.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the phone's settings showing 'SIM status' or 'Network' with 'Unlocked' or 'No SIM restrictions'.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially locked or restricted.

proof_requests: A clear photo or video of the phone's settings menu showing the exact model name.
A video of the phone folding and unfolding smoothly.
A screenshot of the phone's network settings showing it is unlocked.
A close-up of the box showing any model number or text.
response.reason: The seller claims a non-existent model ('Pixel 10 Pro Fold'), and no model name is visible in the photos. The phone appears to be a foldable Google device, but without proof of the exact model, it cannot be priced as a premium Pixel. The risks of misrepresentation, damage, or lock status require further verification before pricing.
